questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Maya buys a car priced at $24,000 in New Jersey, where sales tax is 6.625%. In this example, tax applies to the price only. How much is the sales tax?
questions.intro: Buying a car costs more than its price. Sales tax is a percent of the price: tax = price × rate as a decimal. New Jersey's rate is 6.625% (0.06625).
questions.topic: The total cost of buying a car

misconceptions.C: Uses 66.25% because the decimal moved the wrong way
misconceptions.D: Gives the price plus tax instead of the tax

sources: New Jersey Division of Taxation: The New Jersey sales tax rate has been 6.625% since January 1, 2018. (https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: A car is priced at $24,000. Tax is $1,590, the dealer documentation fee is $399, and title and registration cost $260. What is the out-the-door price?
questions.intro: The out-the-door price is the total you pay to drive away: vehicle price + sales tax + dealer fees + title and registration + any add-ons.
questions.topic: The total cost of buying a car

misconceptions.C: Adds the tax but leaves out both fees
misconceptions.A: Treats the price tag as the full cost

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: A salesperson asks, "What monthly payment do you want?" Why is it smarter to negotiate the out-the-door price?

choices.text: A low payment can hide a higher price
Monthly payments include no interest, so they show the true cost
Dealers are not allowed to change a price once a payment is named
Talking about price is rude, so the payment is a friendlier way to agree

questions.correct_answer: A low payment can hide a higher price
questions.intro: A payment depends on price, rate, and loan length. A dealer can meet any payment target by stretching the loan or raising the price, so agree on the total price first, then discuss financing.
questions.feedback: Negotiate the total price; a longer loan can make a higher price look affordable.
questions.topic: The total cost of buying a car

misconceptions.B: Believes a payment contains no interest
misconceptions.C: Invents a rule that does not exist

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: In a state with no extra used-car warranty law, a used car's Buyers Guide is checked "AS IS - NO DEALER WARRANTY." What does that mean?

choices.text: The dealer must fix any problem for one full year after the sale
The car has passed a state inspection that guarantees its condition
The buyer pays for repairs after the sale
The price is final and the dealer will not negotiate it at all

questions.correct_answer: The buyer pays for repairs after the sale
questions.intro: Federal rules require dealers to post a Buyers Guide on used cars. It says whether the car comes with a warranty or is sold "as is." Some states, including New Jersey, require a limited warranty on many used cars, so check your state's rules.
questions.feedback: "As is" means no dealer warranty: repairs after the sale are the buyer's cost.
questions.topic: The total cost of buying a car

misconceptions.B: Confuses a sticker with an inspection

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Before buying a used car from a private seller, which step best protects Maya?

choices.text: Pay for an independent mechanic's inspection
Trust the seller's description because they have owned it for years
Skip the test drive so the car does not get more miles on it
Judge the condition from the photos in the online listing

questions.correct_answer: Pay for an independent mechanic's inspection
questions.intro: A pre-purchase inspection by a mechanic you choose costs a little and can reveal expensive problems. Also take a test drive and check the vehicle history report.
questions.feedback: An independent inspection finds problems the seller may not mention.
questions.topic: The total cost of buying a car

misconceptions.B: Relies on the seller, who wants a sale
misconceptions.C: Gives up the chance to notice problems

questions.prompt: What is a certified pre-owned (CPO) car?

choices.text: A brand-new car that has never been registered to anyone
A used car whose price is set by the government
A used car inspected and backed by a warranty
Any used car sold by a private seller with a receipt

questions.correct_answer: A used car inspected and backed by a warranty
questions.intro: CPO programs, usually run by manufacturers, inspect late-model used cars and add an extended warranty, at a higher price than a regular used car.
questions.feedback: CPO cars are inspected used cars with an added warranty.

questions.prompt: A vehicle history report shows a "salvage" title. What does that mean?

choices.text: An insurer once declared it a total loss
The car has had only one careful owner since it was new
The car was built with recycled parts to protect the environment
The car qualifies for a lower sales tax rate

questions.correct_answer: An insurer once declared it a total loss
questions.intro: History reports (from services such as Carfax or AutoCheck) show past accidents, title brands such as salvage or flood, and odometer readings.
questions.feedback: A salvage title means the car was once a total loss; it may have hidden damage and lower resale value.

questions.prompt: Sam's current car is worth $6,000 as a trade-in, but Sam still owes $8,000 on its loan. What is Sam's negative equity?
questions.intro: Equity = value − amount owed. When you owe more than the car is worth, the difference is negative equity ("being underwater").
